summary: Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg (ca. 2006–2017) under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk (ca. 2012–2017) and became a professor at the University of Leipzig around 2022.

Dagpo Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and later taught David Seyfort Ruegg and Anne-Marie Blondeau, among others.

Taichi Tado specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. His appointments include positions as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2020) and lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Daiei Kaneko was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University (ca. 1898–1904) and under Manshi Kiyozawa (ca. 1901–1903). He held posts at Toyo University and Otani University (ca. 1916–1951), and founded Koho Gakuen.
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies researcher who studied as a research student (kenkyūsei) at Ryukoku University, an affiliation attested in 2006.

Daijaku Judith Kinst is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She served as a faculty member at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held teaching posts at Taisho University (part-time lecturer attested 2015; instructor attested 2026) and served as a full-time lecturer in sectarian studies at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Daijō Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, later serving there as lecturer and professor (1925–1931), as professor at Toyo University (1931), and at the Academy of Oriental Culture.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Eihei-ji, Komazawa University, and under Daicho Hayashi and Ekō Hashimoto. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission, San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and Hokyoji Zen Practice Community.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Kōsen Imakita, Soyen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held professorships at Otani University (1921–1960) and Columbia University (1952–1957), and also taught at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo.

Daishun Ueyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as associate professor (ca. 1969–1978), professor (ca. 1978–1999), and president (ca. 1995–1999).

Daito Shimaji was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University, and taught at Toyo University (ca. 1906–1927), the University of Tokyo (1923), Komazawa University, and Rissho University.

Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and served as the David B. and Mary H. Gamble Professor at Occidental College (ca. 1980–2017).

Dalsukh Malvania was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (ca. 1948–1956), served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (ca. 1957–1977), and held appointments at the University of Toronto and MSU Baroda.
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford, he held appointments at Goldsmiths, University of London from ca. 1990 to 2013, where he became Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff. He held academic posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

Dan Arnold is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Columbia University, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago, he taught at McGill University (2003–2004) and the University of Chicago (2004–2011).
Dan Li is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso. She holds an appointment as Associate Professor at Soka University (attested 2026).
